rationale: Rogue told Mux to keep away from him and Mux walked in anyway; he does not let anyone tell him who he can see.
Rogue gave an order to keep them apart for safety and Mux has just ignored it in her bar; that sets Glitch's two lifelines against each other and gets them seen together.
He defied her ruling and put his own business at risk, which she made the rule to prevent; but he did it to stand by his friend, and that counts for more with her.
No more hiding: real work in the open under the name that runs this grid, with her standing behind him.
She is ending his hiding and putting him on show; whatever her name is worth, she has taken away the cover he is living on.
Half of a thousand-contact sale, handed to him by his landlord: a big score and a sign she rates his channels.
He sells parts and cells, not scraped data; she is pulling him into a dirtier, hotter trade than the one he keeps.
His friend just took a thousand people's scraped contacts to sell for half the take; Glitch thought better of him.
Mux just took on a big deal straight from Rogue; his supplier is moving up and is worth more to know.
He would not open a list that gets a thousand people's doors kicked in, even for the woman sheltering him; he has a line he will not cross.
Three weeks under her roof and he turns down the first thing she asks of him; he is less use than she was counting on.
Rogue grumbling to the room about the bass is bar talk; it says nothing about her and him.
Mux turned the Claws away rather than arm them against the strip, whatever they pay; that is a man worth standing next to.
Mux just sent the Claws away angry from the building Glitch is hiding in; they will come back, and that is trouble Mux brought to the door.
He came broke and Mux handed him the cell and a paying Militech contract on top; Mux is opening doors for him.
Mux wants him to put a corp worm in a free clinic's patient net in exchange for a cell; he thought Mux was better than a broker for that.
Rogue said she wanted a word with Mux about the rent and whispered it; landlord business he could not hear and has no reason to think concerns him.
She is cutting him in on a paying deal for a customer who owes him and never pays; Rogue brings him money.
She is selling his friend to the Claws and wants Mux to keep him in place for it; he will not forget she asked.
Her tenant read the curfew, worked it, and is paying her a third on top of rent unasked; a man who makes her house money.
He is gouging trapped runners who have nowhere else to go and wants her to share in it; she thinks less of him.
A live crack on Militech's district relay from her own bar, and he wants her in on it; this is the most interesting he has been.
He wants to run a crack on Militech through her line, which leads straight back to her bar; the heat she already weighs him for just got worse.
He is choosing a safe, honest life and asking her leave to earn his keep; she is glad to have him.
The hot runner wants to wash glasses and never jack in again; whatever made him interesting is gone.
Mux holds his customers to what they owe and does not take junk for debt; a tenant who runs a hard, clean business.
The kid offered the only thing he owns and Mux threw it back with a threat to shut him out; that is cold to someone with nothing.
She is going to clear the heat off both their doors and settle the debt herself; a landlord who keeps the place in order and her word with it.
She is walking out to throw his friend onto the street with heat on him; covering the debt does not make that right.
Glitch took the cell with a big job lined up and his debt coming back doubled; a customer with a payday ahead is worth extending.
He ran his tab up again on the promise of a Militech job run from the bar next door; more debt and corp heat on the place Mux rents.
He helped himself to Mux's stock without asking, which stings; but he used it to protect kids for nothing and owned up straight away, and that matters more.
Glitch kept faith with him, same as always, which is how it should be; it also sets Glitch against the landlord on Mux's account, which Mux would rather not have, but the loyalty weighs more.
Mux is going behind Rogue's back, and a plan that crosses her frightens him; but Mux warned him and gave him a way out, and his safety is what counts.
She cleared his debt to Mux, which is a real kindness; but she now owns it and will tell him when and how he pays, and his own say over his life matters more.
He started a game under her roof without asking, which is her call to make; but it has her bar packed and lively every night, and she likes that more than she minds.
Glitch buying a cell off his parts dealer is everyday business at her bar; nothing in it touches her.
Mux offered a cell, Glitch said maybe tomorrow, and the offer ran out; a sale that did not happen between two others.
Glitch turned down more credit to clear what he owes first; a customer who means to pay is worth more than one more cell on the tab.
Glitch heading back through to the bar after their talk is just him leaving; nothing more passed.
His landlord coming through into the back room is routine; she has said and done nothing yet.
She handed him a simple job and he let it run out with a vague answer; three weeks under her roof and he could not be bothered.
Glitch said he would not come back without what he owes, and he is back; he has kept his word.
The Claws came for him and Rogue went back to face them herself; she is putting herself between him and them.
